newsitem.title: NORWAY: Bad weather halts N.Sea oil loadings, output cut.
newsitem.headline: Bad weather halts N.Sea oil loadings, output cut.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Monday bad weather had halted offshore oil loadings at the North Sea Statfjord and Gullfaks fields.
Statoil said crude production at the developments was down to "a bare minimum."
Saga Petroleum ASA, operator of the Snorre, Tordis and Vigdis installations that feed crude to Statfjord and Gullfaks, said it had completely shut in output at the fields.
Statoil spokeswoman Nina Steihaug said offshore crude loadings were halted late on Friday.
"We had to reduce production because of storage space. At the moment production is just barely keeping the systems warm," she said.

Statfjord pumps about 380,000 barrel per day (bpd) and processes crude from the Statfjord East and North satellites and the nearby Snorre and Vigdis developments, which in total add roughly 400,000 bpd to the Statfjord stream.
Gullfaks produces around 475,000 bpd and handles around 85,000 bpd of output from the Tordis field.
Saga spokesman Bjoern Schibevaag said pumping at Snorre, Vigdis and Tordis was stopped on Sunday.
"But we're hoping there will be a weather window today some time between 3 p.m. (1400 GMT) and 6 p.m. (1700 GMT)," he said.
North Sea loadings are often disrupted in winter when high winds and swell prevent the shuttle tankers from attaching to the offshore loading buoys.
